people.solomon.role: King who builds the temple and later turns away
people.solomon.meaning: David has him anointed king at Gihon. He asks God for an understanding heart and builds the temple. Later his wives turn his heart to other gods. The LORD says he will tear the kingdom from Solomon’s son.
people.adonijah.meaning: He says, “I will be king,” and holds a feast with Joab and Abiathar. The feast ends when Solomon is anointed. Later he asks for Abishag as his wife. Solomon has Benaiah kill him.
people.abishag.relations: She serves King David. Adonijah later asks to marry her.
people.abishag.meaning: She is brought to keep the old king warm, and she serves him. After David dies, Adonijah asks Bathsheba to get her as his wife. Solomon hears the request as a claim on the kingdom and has Adonijah killed.
people.judgment-women.role: Two unnamed women who both claim one baby
people.judgment-women.relations: Both live in one house, and each has a baby. The text calls them prostitutes.
people.judgment-women.meaning: One woman’s baby dies in the night. Each tells Solomon the living child is hers. Solomon calls for a sword to cut the child in two. One woman begs him to let the child live, and Solomon names her the mother.
people.pharaoh-daughter-solomon.relation: Daughter of Pharaoh and wife of Solomon. She is not the princess who finds Moses.
people.pharaoh-daughter-solomon.meaning: Solomon marries her to join with Pharaoh king of Egypt. She lives in David’s city until Solomon builds her a house. Pharaoh gives her the city of Gezer as a wedding gift.
people.adoniram.meaning: He is over the men Solomon forces to work. Solomon sends thirty thousand of them to Lebanon in turns. He may be the Adoram of chapter 12, but that is a proposal.
people.hiram-artisan.role: Bronze worker who makes the temple pieces
people.hiram-artisan.relations: His mother is a widow of Naphtali. His father is a bronze worker of Tyre. He is not King Hiram.
people.hiram-artisan.meaning: Solomon brings him from Tyre. He casts the two bronze pillars, the sea, and the ten bases. He also makes the pots, shovels, and basins for the LORD’s house.
people.queen-sheba.role: Unnamed queen who tests Solomon with questions
people.queen-sheba.relations: She visits Solomon from her own land with her servants.
people.queen-sheba.meaning: She hears of Solomon’s fame and comes to test him with hard questions. He answers them all. She praises his wisdom and blesses the LORD. She gives him gold, spices, and precious stones, then goes home.
people.hadad-edom.role: Edomite royal child who flees to Egypt
people.hadad-edom.relations: One of the king’s offspring in Edom. Husband of Tahpenes’s sister and father of Genubath.
people.hadad-edom.meaning: Joab kills the males of Edom, and the child Hadad flees to Egypt. Pharaoh gives him a house, land, and a wife. When David and Joab die, he asks Pharaoh to let him go home. The LORD raises him as an enemy of Solomon.
people.rezon.role: Enemy of Solomon who rules in Damascus
people.rezon.relations: Son of Eliada. He flees from his lord, Hadadezer king of Zobah.
people.rezon.meaning: He gathers men and leads a troop. They settle in Damascus, and he rules Syria. He is an enemy to Israel all the days of Solomon.
people.jeroboam.role: First king of the northern tribes
people.jeroboam.meaning: Solomon puts him over the labor of the house of Joseph. Ahijah tears a garment and promises him ten tribes. He flees to Egypt, returns, and becomes king of Israel. He then makes two gold calves so the people will not go to Jerusalem.
people.ahijah-shiloh.role: Prophet who promises Jeroboam ten tribes
people.ahijah-shiloh.relations: From Shiloh. He is not the scribe Ahijah or Baasha’s father Ahijah.
people.ahijah-shiloh.meaning: He tears a new garment into twelve pieces and gives Jeroboam ten. The ten pieces stand for ten tribes. Later he is old and cannot see. He still knows Jeroboam’s disguised wife and says her child will die.
people.rehoboam.meaning: The people ask him at Shechem to make their work lighter. He drops the old men’s advice and promises a heavier yoke. Israel turns from him, and he keeps Judah. In his fifth year Shishak takes the temple treasures.
people.shishak.role: King of Egypt who attacks Jerusalem
people.shishak.relations: Jeroboam flees to him. He later attacks Rehoboam’s city.
people.shishak.meaning: Jeroboam stays in Egypt with him until Solomon dies. In Rehoboam’s fifth year he comes against Jerusalem. He takes the treasures of the LORD’s house and the king’s house. He also takes Solomon’s gold shields.
people.tahpenes.role: Queen of Egypt in Hadad’s story
people.tahpenes.relations: Wife of Pharaoh. Her sister marries Hadad.
people.tahpenes.meaning: Pharaoh gives her sister to Hadad as wife. Tahpenes weans their son Genubath in Pharaoh’s house. The text says nothing more about her.
people.genubath.relations: Son of Hadad. His mother is the sister of Tahpenes.
people.genubath.meaning: Tahpenes weans him in Pharaoh’s house. He lives there among Pharaoh’s sons. The text names him in one verse and tells no more.
people.shemaiah.role: Man of God who stops Rehoboam’s war
people.shemaiah.relations: He speaks to Rehoboam, Judah, and Benjamin.
people.shemaiah.meaning: Rehoboam gathers 180,000 warriors to win Israel back. Shemaiah gives God’s word: do not fight your brothers. The men listen and go home.
people.adoram.relations: He serves Rehoboam. He may be the Adoniram of chapters 4 and 5, but that is a proposal.
people.adoram.meaning: He is over the men forced to work. Rehoboam sends him after Israel turns away. All Israel stones him to death, and Rehoboam flees to Jerusalem in his chariot.
people.judah-man-god.role: Unnamed man of God who speaks against Bethel’s altar
people.judah-man-god.relations: He comes from Judah. He faces Jeroboam and then meets the old prophet of Bethel.
people.judah-man-god.meaning: He cries out against Jeroboam’s altar, and the altar splits. Jeroboam’s hand dries up, and the man prays until it is healed. He was told not to eat or drink there. An old prophet lies to him, and he eats. A lion kills him on the road.
people.bethel-old-prophet.role: Unnamed old prophet who lies to the man of God
people.bethel-old-prophet.relations: He lives in Bethel. His sons tell him what the man of God did.
people.bethel-old-prophet.meaning: He rides after the man of God. He lies that an angel said to bring him home. At the table he speaks the LORD’s word against his guest. Later he buries the man in his own grave.
people.jeroboam-wife.relations: Wife of Jeroboam. Mother of the sick child Abijah.
people.jeroboam-wife.meaning: Jeroboam sends her to Shiloh in disguise with bread, cakes, and honey. Ahijah cannot see, yet he knows her at the door. He gives her heavy news for Jeroboam’s house. She reaches Tirzah, and the child dies as she steps in.
people.abijah-child.meaning: He falls sick, and his mother goes to ask Ahijah about him. He dies when she comes home. All Israel buries him and mourns. He is not Abijam, the king of Judah.
people.naamah.relations: Mother of Rehoboam. The text calls her the Ammonitess.
people.naamah.meaning: The text names her twice as Rehoboam’s mother. It tells nothing that she does.
people.abijam.meaning: He rules three years in Jerusalem. He walks in his father’s sins and is at war with Jeroboam. The LORD still gives him a son to rule after him, for David’s sake.
people.asa.role: King of Judah who removes idols and pays Syria
people.asa.relations: Son of Abijam. Father of Jehoshaphat.
people.asa.meaning: He removes the idols and removes Maacah from being queen. The high places stay. When Baasha builds Ramah, Asa sends the temple’s silver and gold to Ben Hadad. Ben Hadad attacks Israel, and Asa builds Geba and Mizpah with Ramah’s stones.
people.maacah-queen.relations: Daughter of Abishalom. The text calls her mother of Abijam and of Asa.
people.maacah-queen.meaning: She makes an image for an Asherah. Asa removes her from being queen. He cuts down her image and burns it at the brook Kidron.
people.ben-hadad-asa.role: King of Syria paid to attack Israel
people.ben-hadad-asa.relations: Son of Tabrimmon, son of Hezion. The Ben Hadad who fights Ahab in chapter 20 appears to be a later king.
people.ben-hadad-asa.meaning: Asa sends him silver and gold and asks him to break his treaty with Baasha. He agrees. His captains strike Ijon, Dan, Abel Beth Maacah, and the land of Naphtali. Baasha then stops building Ramah.
people.nadab.role: King of Israel killed by Baasha
people.nadab.meaning: He rules Israel two years and walks in his father’s way. Baasha kills him while Israel attacks Gibbethon. Baasha then kills all the house of Jeroboam.
people.baasha.role: King of Israel who kills Nadab
people.baasha.relations: Son of Ahijah of Issachar, who is not the prophet Ahijah. Father of Elah.
people.baasha.meaning: He kills Nadab at Gibbethon and wipes out Jeroboam’s house. He rules from Tirzah for twenty-four years and fights Asa. He builds Ramah but stops when Ben Hadad attacks. Jehu the son of Hanani tells him his own house will fall.
people.jehu-hanani.role: Prophet who speaks against Baasha’s house
people.jehu-hanani.relations: Son of Hanani. He is not Jehu the son of Nimshi.
people.jehu-hanani.meaning: He brings the LORD’s word against Baasha. Baasha walked in Jeroboam’s way, so his house will be swept away. Zimri later kills all the house of Baasha, as Jehu said.
people.elah.role: King of Israel killed by his officer
people.elah.meaning: He rules Israel two years in Tirzah. He is drinking in Arza’s house when Zimri strikes him dead. Zimri then kills all the house of Baasha.
people.zimri.role: Chariot officer who rules for seven days
people.zimri.relations: Servant of Elah and captain of half his chariots. Omri’s army comes against him.
people.zimri.meaning: He kills Elah and all the house of Baasha. The army hears and makes Omri king. Omri takes Tirzah. Zimri burns the king’s house over himself and dies after seven days.
people.omri.meaning: The army makes him king in the camp at Gibbethon. He takes Tirzah from Zimri and then beats Tibni’s side. He buys a hill from Shemer and builds Samaria. The text says he did more evil than all before him.
people.tibni.role: Rival of Omri for the throne
people.tibni.meaning: Half the people follow Tibni to make him king. Half follow Omri. Omri’s side wins, Tibni dies, and Omri rules. The text does not say how Tibni dies.
people.shemer.role: Owner of the hill of Samaria
people.shemer.relations: He sells his hill to Omri.
people.shemer.meaning: Omri buys the hill from him for two talents of silver. Omri builds a city there and names it Samaria after Shemer.
people.ahab.role: King of Israel faced by Elijah and Micaiah
people.ahab.meaning: He marries Jezebel and builds an altar for Baal in Samaria. He beats Ben Hadad twice but lets him go. He takes Naboth’s vineyard after Jezebel has Naboth killed. He ignores Micaiah’s warning and dies of an arrow wound at Ramoth Gilead.
people.jezebel.role: Queen who threatens Elijah and has Naboth killed
people.jezebel.meaning: She cuts off the LORD’s prophets. After Carmel she swears to kill Elijah. She writes letters in Ahab’s name so Naboth is accused and stoned. The LORD says dogs will eat her by Jezreel’s wall.
people.hiel.role: Man of Bethel who builds Jericho
people.hiel.meaning: He builds Jericho in Ahab’s days. He lays its base at the loss of Abiram, his firstborn. He sets up its gates at the loss of Segub, his youngest. The text says this matches the LORD’s word by Joshua.
people.elijah.role: Prophet who stands against Ahab and Baal
people.elijah.relations: A Tishbite from the settlers of Gilead. He calls Elisha to follow him.
people.elijah.meaning: He tells Ahab no rain will fall, then hides at Cherith and Zarephath. On Mount Carmel he prays, fire falls, and he kills the prophets of Baal. He runs from Jezebel to Horeb, where the LORD gives him new work. He later tells Ahab his house will fall for Naboth’s death.
people.zarephath-widow.relations: Mother of a son who falls sick and lives again.
people.zarephath-widow.meaning: She has one handful of meal and a little oil. She bakes for Elijah first, and the jars do not run out. When her son stops breathing, she blames Elijah. Elijah gives him back alive, and she calls Elijah a man of God.
people.zarephath-son.role: Unnamed boy whom Elijah’s prayer brings back
people.zarephath-son.meaning: He falls sick until no breath is left in him. Elijah stretches over him three times and cries to the LORD. The child’s soul comes back, and Elijah gives him to his mother.
people.obadiah-palace.role: Palace official who hides the LORD’s prophets
people.obadiah-palace.relations: He is over Ahab’s household and fears the LORD greatly.
people.obadiah-palace.meaning: He hides one hundred prophets from Jezebel in caves and feeds them. Ahab sends him to look for grass, and he meets Elijah. He fears Ahab will kill him if Elijah is gone. He still goes and tells Ahab.
people.elijah-servant.relations: He serves Elijah. The text does not name him.
people.elijah-servant.meaning: On Carmel, Elijah sends him seven times to look toward the sea. The seventh time he sees a small cloud like a man’s hand. Elijah sends him to warn Ahab of rain. Elijah later leaves his servant at Beersheba.
people.elisha.role: Farmer whom Elijah calls with his mantle
people.elisha.meaning: The LORD tells Elijah to anoint him prophet in Elijah’s place. Elijah finds him plowing with twelve yoke of oxen and puts his mantle on him. Elisha kills his oxen, feeds the people, and follows Elijah. His later work is in 2 Kings.
people.hazael.role: Man the LORD names as Syria’s next king
people.hazael.relations: The LORD names him to Elijah at Horeb, with Jehu and Elisha.
people.hazael.meaning: The LORD tells Elijah to anoint Hazael king over Syria. The LORD speaks of the sword of Hazael. Hazael does nothing in this book. His rise is told in 2 Kings.
people.jehu-nimshi.role: Man the LORD names as Israel’s future king
people.jehu-nimshi.relations: Son of Nimshi. He is not the prophet Jehu the son of Hanani.
people.jehu-nimshi.meaning: The LORD tells Elijah to anoint Jehu king over Israel. Jehu will kill those who escape Hazael’s sword. He does nothing in this book. 2 Kings tells how he takes power.
people.ben-hadad-ahab.role: King of Syria beaten and freed by Ahab
people.ben-hadad-ahab.relations: Thirty-two kings march with him. He appears to be a later king than Asa’s ally Ben Hadad.
people.ben-hadad-ahab.meaning: He attacks Samaria and demands Ahab’s silver, gold, wives, and children. Israel beats him while he is drinking. The next year he loses again at Aphek and hides in an inner room. Ahab calls him brother, makes a covenant, and lets him go.
people.ahab-prophets.role: Unnamed prophets who speak to Ahab in chapter 20
people.ahab-prophets.relations: They speak to Ahab during the wars with Ben Hadad. They are not the four hundred prophets of chapter 22.
people.ahab-prophets.meaning: A prophet tells Ahab the LORD will give him the great army. A man of God promises a second win at Aphek. After Ahab frees Ben Hadad, one of the prophets waits for him in disguise. He tells Ahab his life will pay for the man he let go.
people.naboth.relations: A man of Jezreel. His vineyard lies next to Ahab’s palace.
people.naboth.meaning: Ahab offers to buy or trade for his vineyard. Naboth says he will not give up the land of his fathers. Jezebel has two men accuse him of cursing God and the king. He is stoned to death, and Ahab goes to take the vineyard.
people.jehoshaphat.role: King of Judah who asks for the LORD’s word
people.jehoshaphat.meaning: He agrees to go with Ahab to Ramoth Gilead. He asks for the LORD’s word first, and then for one more prophet. In battle the Syrians take him for Ahab until he cries out. He rules Judah twenty-five years and makes peace with Israel.
people.micaiah.role: Prophet who warns Ahab before battle
people.micaiah.relations: Son of Imlah. Ahab hates him and puts him in prison.
people.micaiah.meaning: Told to agree with the other prophets, he first says, “Go up and prosper.” Ahab demands the truth. He tells of Israel scattered like sheep and of a lying spirit the LORD sent. Zedekiah strikes him, and Ahab sends him to prison.
people.zedekiah-chenaanah.relations: Son of Chenaanah. He is not the later king of Judah named Zedekiah.
people.zedekiah-chenaanah.meaning: He makes iron horns and says Ahab will push the Syrians with them. When Micaiah speaks of a lying spirit, he strikes Micaiah on the cheek. Micaiah says he will hide in an inner room.
people.amon-governor.relations: He is named with Joash the king’s son. He is not the later king of Judah named Amon.
people.amon-governor.meaning: Ahab orders Micaiah taken back to him. He is to keep Micaiah in prison on bread and water until Ahab returns. The text names him in one verse.
people.joash-prince.role: King’s son told to hold Micaiah
people.joash-prince.relations: Called the king’s son. He is named with Amon the governor.
people.joash-prince.meaning: Ahab sends Micaiah back to him and to Amon. They are to keep Micaiah in prison until Ahab returns in peace. The text names him in one verse.
people.ahaziah-ahab.meaning: He becomes king in Samaria and rules two years. He asks to send his servants in Jehoshaphat’s ships, and Jehoshaphat refuses. He serves Baal as his father did. His story goes on in 2 Kings.
people.joab.meaning: He helps Adonijah and eats at his feast. David tells Solomon that Joab killed Abner and Amasa in peace time. When Adonijah dies, Joab flees to the altar. Benaiah kills him there on Solomon’s order.
people.nathan-prophet.role: Prophet who helps Solomon become king
people.nathan-prophet.relations: He speaks to Bathsheba and to David. He works with Zadok and Benaiah.
people.nathan-prophet.meaning: He tells Bathsheba that Adonijah is acting as king. He sends her to David and then comes in to back her words. David orders Solomon made king. Nathan and Zadok anoint Solomon at Gihon.
people.hiram.role: King of Tyre who sends Solomon wood and gold
people.hiram.relations: He always loved David and makes a treaty with Solomon. He is not Hiram the bronze worker.
people.hiram.meaning: He sends Solomon cedar and cypress wood, and Solomon pays in wheat and oil. Solomon gives him twenty cities in Galilee, and they do not please him. His sailors go with Solomon’s ships to Ophir for gold.
people.zadok.meaning: He does not join Adonijah. At David’s order he takes the horn of oil from the Tent and anoints Solomon. Solomon then puts him in Abiathar’s place as priest.
people.benaiah.role: Officer who carries out Solomon’s death orders
people.benaiah.meaning: He does not join Adonijah and helps bring Solomon to Gihon. On Solomon’s orders he kills Adonijah, Joab, and Shimei. Solomon puts him over the army in Joab’s place.
people.bathsheba.role: Solomon’s mother who speaks for him to David
people.bathsheba.meaning: Nathan warns her, and she reminds David of his oath that Solomon will rule. David swears it again that day. Later Adonijah asks her to seek Abishag for him. She carries the request to Solomon, and Solomon has Adonijah killed.
people.shimei-gera.role: Benjamite told not to leave Jerusalem
people.shimei-gera.meaning: David tells Solomon that Shimei once cursed him. Solomon orders Shimei to stay in Jerusalem or die. After three years Shimei goes to Gath to bring back two slaves. Solomon has Benaiah kill him.
people.jonathan-abiathar.relations: Son of Abiathar the priest. He brings news to Adonijah.
people.jonathan-abiathar.meaning: He comes to Adonijah’s feast as the trumpet sounds. Adonijah expects good news. Jonathan says David has made Solomon king and Solomon sits on the throne. The guests are afraid and leave.
people.amasa.relations: Son of Jether. His mother Abigail is the sister of Zeruiah.
people.amasa.meaning: He does not act in this book. David tells Solomon that Joab killed him and Abner. Solomon gives this as a reason for Joab’s death.
people.barzillai.relations: A Gileadite. His sons came to David when David fled from Absalom.
people.barzillai.meaning: He does not act in this book. David tells Solomon to show kindness to his sons. They are to eat at Solomon’s table.
people.abner.relations: Son of Ner. Captain of the army of Israel.
people.abner.meaning: He does not act in this book. David tells Solomon that Joab killed him and Amasa. Solomon calls both men better than Joab.
people.abiathar.relations: Son of Ahimelech and father of Jonathan. He carried the ark before David.
people.abiathar.meaning: He helps Adonijah and eats at his feast. Solomon says he deserves death but spares him for his service to David. Solomon ends his work as priest and sends him to Anathoth. Chapter 4 still lists him as a priest.
people.david.meaning: He is old and cold when Adonijah claims the throne. Bathsheba and Nathan remind him of his oath, and he has Solomon anointed. He tells Solomon to keep God’s law and to deal with Joab and Shimei. After his death the LORD spares part of the kingdom for his sake.
places.gath.summary: Two of Shimei’s slaves run away to Achish, king of Gath, in chapter 2. Shimei goes there and brings them back. Solomon has him killed for leaving Jerusalem.
places.gath.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.beersheba.summary: Elijah runs from Jezebel to Beersheba in chapter 19. He leaves his servant there and walks on into the wilderness.
places.beersheba.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.jerusalem.summary: David has Solomon made king here in chapter 1. Solomon builds the temple and his own house here. Shishak takes the city’s treasures in chapter 14.
places.jerusalem.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.gibeon.summary: Solomon offers sacrifices at Gibeon in chapter 3. The LORD appears to him there in a dream. Solomon asks for an understanding heart.
places.gibeon.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.tyre.summary: Hiram is king of Tyre. He sends Solomon cedar and cypress wood in chapter 5. Solomon brings Hiram the bronze worker from Tyre in chapter 7.
places.tyre.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.gezer.summary: Pharaoh takes Gezer, burns it, and gives it to his daughter in chapter 9. She is Solomon’s wife. Solomon then builds Gezer with forced labor.
places.gezer.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.edom.summary: Joab kills the males of Edom in David’s time. The child Hadad, of Edom’s royal family, flees to Egypt. In chapter 11 the LORD raises Hadad against Solomon.
places.edom.limits: The marker stands for a wide region, not one spot.
places.jericho.summary: Hiel the Bethelite builds Jericho in chapter 16. He loses his firstborn and his youngest son. The chapter says this matches the LORD’s word by Joshua.
places.jericho.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.en-rogel.summary: Adonijah kills sheep and cattle by a stone beside En Rogel in chapter 1. He invites his brothers to the feast but not Solomon.
places.en-rogel.limits: The marker shows a proposed site for the spring.
places.gilead.summary: Gilead lies east of the Jordan. Elijah the Tishbite is one of its settlers in chapter 17.
places.gilead.limits: The marker stands for a wide region, not one spot.
places.dan.summary: Jeroboam puts one gold calf in Dan in chapter 12. The people go as far as Dan to worship before it.
places.dan.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location in the north.
places.sidon.summary: Jezebel is the daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians. Ahab marries her in chapter 16 and serves Baal.
places.sidon.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.gihon.summary: Zadok and Nathan anoint Solomon king at Gihon in chapter 1. The people blow the trumpet and shout, “Long live King Solomon!”
places.gihon.limits: The marker shows the general location of this spring at Jerusalem.
places.anathoth.summary: Solomon sends Abiathar the priest to his fields at Anathoth in chapter 2. Abiathar had helped Adonijah. Solomon spares his life but ends his work as priest.
places.anathoth.limits: The marker shows a proposed site. The exact place is not certain.
places.lebanon.summary: Solomon asks Hiram for cedar trees from Lebanon in chapter 5. Solomon sends thirty thousand men there in turns to work.
places.lebanon.limits: The marker stands for a wide mountain region, not one spot.
places.succoth.summary: The bronze pieces for the temple are cast in clay ground between Succoth and Zarethan. Chapter 7 puts this ground in the plain of the Jordan.
places.succoth.limits: The marker shows a proposed site. The exact place is not certain.
places.zarethan.summary: The bronze pieces for the temple are cast in clay ground between Succoth and Zarethan. Chapter 7 puts this ground in the plain of the Jordan.
places.zarethan.limits: The town’s location is not certain. The marker shows a general area.
places.galilee.summary: Solomon gives Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee in chapter 9. Hiram comes from Tyre to see them, and they do not please him.
places.galilee.limits: The marker stands for a wide region, not one spot.
places.hazor.summary: Solomon uses forced labor to build Hazor in chapter 9. The same list names Megiddo and Gezer.
places.hazor.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.megiddo.summary: Solomon uses forced labor to build Megiddo in chapter 9. The same list names Hazor and Gezer.
places.megiddo.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.ezion-geber.summary: Solomon builds ships at Ezion Geber in chapter 9. It is beside Eloth on the Red Sea, in the land of Edom. Jehoshaphat’s ships wreck there in chapter 22.
places.ezion-geber.limits: Its site on the Gulf of Aqaba is disputed. The marker shows a general area.
places.egypt.summary: Hadad and Jeroboam each flee to Egypt in chapter 11. Shishak king of Egypt attacks Jerusalem in chapter 14.
places.egypt.limits: The marker stands for a wide region, not one spot.
places.damascus.summary: Rezon and his men settle in Damascus and rule there in chapter 11. In chapter 15 Ben Hadad lives there. Asa sends him silver and gold.
places.damascus.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.shiloh.summary: Ahijah the prophet is called the Shilonite in chapter 11. Jeroboam’s wife goes to his house in Shiloh in chapter 14.
places.shiloh.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.zeredah.summary: Jeroboam the son of Nebat is an Ephraimite of Zeredah. Chapter 11 names the town once.
places.zeredah.limits: The town’s location is not certain. The marker shows a general area.
places.shechem.summary: All Israel comes to Shechem to make Rehoboam king in chapter 12. The people ask for lighter work, and he refuses. Jeroboam later builds Shechem and lives there.
places.shechem.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.bethel.summary: Jeroboam sets a gold calf and an altar in Bethel in chapter 12. A man of God from Judah speaks against the altar in chapter 13. An old prophet who lives in Bethel buries him.
places.bethel.limits: The marker shows a proposed site. The exact place is not certain.
places.penuel.summary: Jeroboam goes out from Shechem and builds Penuel in chapter 12.
places.penuel.limits: The marker shows a proposed site. The exact place is not certain.
places.tirzah.summary: Jeroboam’s wife comes home to Tirzah in chapter 14, and her child dies. Baasha, Elah, and Zimri rule from Tirzah. Omri attacks it in chapter 16, and Zimri burns the king’s house.
places.tirzah.limits: The marker shows a proposed site. The exact place is not certain.
places.ramah.summary: Baasha builds Ramah to block the way to Asa in chapter 15. He stops when Ben Hadad attacks Israel. Asa’s people carry away its stones and timber.
places.ramah.limits: The marker shows the general location of Ramah in Benjamin.
places.geba.summary: Asa builds Geba of Benjamin with stones and timber from Ramah in chapter 15.
places.geba.limits: The marker shows a proposed site. The exact place is not certain.
places.mizpah.summary: Asa builds Mizpah with stones and timber from Ramah in chapter 15.
places.mizpah.limits: The marker shows a site in Benjamin. That choice is not certain.
places.gibbethon.summary: Gibbethon belongs to the Philistines. Baasha kills Nadab during an attack on it in chapter 15. In chapter 16 the army camped there makes Omri king.
places.gibbethon.limits: The town’s location is not certain. The marker shows a general area.
places.samaria.summary: Omri buys a hill from Shemer and builds Samaria in chapter 16. Ahab rules there and builds a house for Baal. Ben Hadad attacks the city in chapter 20. Ahab is buried there in chapter 22.
places.samaria.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.cherith.summary: Elijah hides by the brook Cherith in chapter 17. Ravens bring him bread and meat. He leaves when the brook dries up.
places.cherith.limits: The exact brook is not known. The marker shows a wide area east of the Jordan.
places.zarephath.summary: The LORD sends Elijah to a widow in Zarephath in chapter 17. Her meal and oil do not run out. Her son stops breathing, and Elijah prays until he lives again.
places.zarephath.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location on the coast.
places.carmel.summary: Elijah meets the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel in chapter 18. The LORD’s fire burns up Elijah’s offering. Elijah then prays on the top, and rain comes.
places.carmel.limits: The marker stands for the whole mountain. The exact spot is not known.
places.kishon.summary: Elijah brings the prophets of Baal down to the brook Kishon in chapter 18. He kills them there.
places.kishon.limits: The marker stands for the river as a whole. The exact spot is not known.
places.jezreel.summary: Ahab rides to Jezreel in the rain in chapter 18, and Elijah runs ahead. Naboth’s vineyard lies next to Ahab’s palace there in chapter 21. Ahab takes it after Naboth is stoned.
places.jezreel.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.horeb.summary: Elijah travels forty days and nights to Horeb, God’s Mountain, in chapter 19. He stays in a cave. The LORD speaks to him there and gives him new work.
places.horeb.limits: The marker follows the traditional Sinai region. The mountain’s location is disputed.
places.abel-meholah.summary: Elisha the son of Shaphat is from Abel Meholah. Elijah finds him plowing in chapter 19 and puts his mantle on him.
places.abel-meholah.limits: The marker shows a proposed site. The exact place is not certain.
places.aphek.summary: Ben Hadad brings the Syrians to Aphek to fight Israel in chapter 20. Israel wins. The Syrians flee into the city, and its wall falls on them.
places.aphek.limits: The location of this battle town is not certain. The marker shows a general area.
places.ramoth-gilead.summary: Ahab and Jehoshaphat go to fight Syria for Ramoth Gilead in chapter 22. An arrow strikes Ahab in the battle, and he dies at evening.
places.ramoth-gilead.limits: The town’s location is disputed. The marker shows a general area.
sources.web.limits: The reading text gives the book’s own account. It cannot by itself check dates, appearances, numbers, or every event.
sources.atlas-canaan.limits: Map positions are estimates for display. A town marker does not prove each event.
sources.terrain.limits: Modern terrain is a map aid. It does not show ancient shorelines or settlements.
sources.yale-solomon.summary: This Yale guide studies royal praise, criticism, and history written to teach about God.
sources.yale-solomon.limits: Its proposed literary sources and its views of Solomon’s economy remain interpretations. They do not prove every action in the account.
sources.yale-division.summary: This Yale guide covers building burdens, the split kingdom, royal shrines, and the northern kings.
sources.yale-division.limits: Its claim that temple building defied God’s instruction is not adopted. Its broad claims about the economy and the time before kings need other evidence.
sources.yale-prophets.summary: This Yale guide covers prophets who oppose royal abuse, and stories of food and healing.
sources.yale-prophets.limits: Use it only for how it frames the stories. Its count of Baal prophets differs from 1 Kings 18:19. It has later reference errors, and it credits Jehu’s actions to Elijah. Those are not adopted.
sources.nelson-record.summary: The edition record names Nelson’s commentary. It says the commentary reads Kings as writing about God.
sources.dm-kings-council.summary: McClellan compares readings of the heavenly council. He questions the idea that the whole Bible teaches one view of God.
sources.lds-kings-solomon.limits: Its older claims about motives and past events are not adopted as verified facts. The bronze sea comparison is Church interpretation.
sources.met-244562.limits: Its form differs from the temple stands described in Kings. It is a comparison and does not show how those stands looked.
chapters.*.mapNote: Points mark named towns and wide regions. Disputed sites and exact buildings are not certain.
chapters.*.routeEvidence: Lines join the named places in story order. They do not show real roads, sea trips, or battle moves.
sources.dm-kings-council.limits: This is an older critical commentary. Porter’s full thesis and House’s commentary were not read. One post does not establish scholarly consensus.
